title: SSRF protection for URL fetchers
when: A server fetches URLs that users supply (link previews, image import, webhook targets, feed readers) and must not become a proxy into private networks.
prompt:
Goal: fetchPublicUrl(url) reaches only public http and https hosts, checked after DNS and on every redirect, with size and time limits.
Steps:
1. Parse with new URL(input); allow http: and https: only, default ports, and no user or password in the URL.
2. Resolve with dns.promises.lookup(host, { all: true }); refuse any loopback (127.0.0.0/8, ::1), private (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, fc00::/7), link local (169.254/16 with the cloud metadata 169.254.169.254, fe80::/10) or 0.0.0.0 address, IPv4 mapped forms included.
3. Connect to the vetted address, not the name again: give http.request a custom lookup returning it, which defeats DNS rebinding.
4. Use redirect: "manual", follow at most 3 hops yourself, and repeat steps 1 to 3 per Location.
5. Limits: AbortSignal.timeout(5000), a byte cap, only the content types the feature needs.
6. Return only what the feature uses (title, image), never raw bodies or internal error text.
Quality bar:
- A domain allowlist wherever the feature allows one.
- Odd IP spellings (2130706433, 0x7f.1) are caught by checking resolved addresses.
- Tests cover each blocked range and a redirect to 127.0.0.1.
Pitfalls:
- Checking the hostname string only.
- Letting fetch follow redirects on its own.
- Echoing the fetched body, which turns blind SSRF into full reads.
Verify:
- [ ] Private, loopback and link local ranges are blocked.
- [ ] Redirect targets are rechecked.
- [ ] Timeout and byte cap exist.
- [ ] Only http and https pass.
Output: safe-fetch.mjs, test/safe-fetch.test.mjs and a note in SECURITY-AUDIT.md.

examples.input: o preview de links do chat busca qualquer URL que o usuario cola
examples.output: scheme check, DNS resolve with private range block, pinned address, manual redirects, 5 s timeout
